# Finding $\det B \cdot (\det A - \det B)$

## Setting Up the Condition

When we replace $a_{ij}$ with $2 - a_{ij}$ to form $A_{ij}$, the determinant changes by:
$$\det(A_{ij}) = \det(A) + (2 - 2a_{ij})C_{ij} = \det(A) + 2(1-a_{ij})C_{ij}$$

where $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}$ is the $(i,j)$-cofactor of $A$.

The condition $\det(A) = \det(A_{ij})$ for all $i,j$ therefore gives:
$$(1 - a_{ij})\,C_{ij} = 0 \quad \text{for all } i,j$$

This means $C_{ij} = a_{ij}\,C_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ (since $C_{ij} - a_{ij}C_{ij} = 0$).

## Expressing $\det B - \det A$

Writing $B = A + \mathbf{v}\mathbf{1}^T$ where $\mathbf{v} = ((-1)^1, (-1)^2, \ldots, (-1)^n)^T$ and $\mathbf{1} = (1,1,\ldots,1)^T$, the matrix determinant lemma gives:
$$\det(B) = \det(A) + \mathbf{1}^T \operatorname{adj}(A)\,\mathbf{v}$$

Since $(\operatorname{adj}(A))_{ij} = C_{ji}$:
$$\det(B) - \det(A) = \sum_{i,j} C_{ji}\,(-1)^j$$

Re-indexing with $p = j$, $q = i$:
$$\det(B) - \det(A) = \sum_{p,q} (-1)^p\, C_{pq}$$

## Applying the Key Condition

Using $C_{pq} = a_{pq}\,C_{pq}$:
$$\det(B) - \det(A) = \sum_{p,q} (-1)^p\, a_{pq}\,C_{pq} = \sum_{p} (-1)^p \underbrace{\sum_{q} a_{pq}\,C_{pq}}_{=\det(A)}$$

$$\det(B) - \det(A) = \det(A)\sum_{p=1}^{n}(-1)^p$$

## Evaluating the Sum

$$\sum_{p=1}^{n}(-1)^p = \begin{cases} 0 & n \text{ even} \\ -1 & n \text{ odd}\end{cases}$$

**Case 1: $n$ even.** Then $\det(B) - \det(A) = \det(A) \cdot 0 = 0$, so $\det(B) = \det(A)$.

**Case 2: $n$ odd.** Then $\det(B) - \det(A) = \det(A)\cdot(-1)$, so $\det(B) = \det(A)(1-1) = 0$.

## Computing the Final Expression

- **If $n$ is even:** $\det B(\det A - \det B) = \det A \cdot (\det A - \det A) = \det A \cdot 0 = 0$

- **If $n$ is odd:** $\det B(\det A - \det B) = 0 \cdot (\det A - 0) = 0$

In both cases the result is zero.

**Verification** ($n=2$, $A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$): $\det A = -1$, $B = \begin{pmatrix}-1&0\\2&1\end{pmatrix}$, $\det B = -1$. Indeed $(-1)(-1-(-1)) = 0$. ✓

$$\boxed{0}$$
